findings.issue: Recovery = manual repeat of PATCH. If the final DB tx fails AGAIN on the retry (e.g. Postgres still down), the KC-disabled+choros-active drift persists and the operator must retry once more — an unbounded operator-driven loop, no background reconciler.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is: it is operator-visible, matches ADR-T0702's own no-job-queue stance, and is explicitly declared out-of-scope in ADR §8 / spec §4б. No change required for this task; note only.

findings.issue: The concurrent-PATCH race defence (§3.3: WHERE deactivated_at IS [NOT] NULL RETURNING id, skip audit on 0 rows) is correct by construction under READ COMMITTED MVCC but is not exercised by a live concurrency test — only the sequential no-op path is tested.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable: a true concurrent-PATCH test is inherently flaky and the MVCC guarantee (second UPDATE re-evaluates WHERE after the first commits → 0 rows → skip audit) is well-established. Left uncovered by design; no action required.

findings.issue: The R-4 warn now also emits to stderr inside the pre-existing FF-702-DEGRADE test (which deliberately fails revoke). Confirmed harmless — expected log noise for a genuinely degraded revoke, no assertion affected, gate still 36/36.
findings.suggestion: No change; this is the intended operator-visibility signal firing exactly when it should.
